title: Formats and what's next
summary: Standard, Commander, building a Commander deck, and where to play.

steps.title: What's a format?
steps.body:
A [[format]] decides which cards and decks are allowed. The core rules stay the same.

This course taught one-against-one play, the way most people learn. Two popular formats build on it:

- **Standard**: two players, recent cards.
- **Commander**: usually four players, big decks with one copy of each card.

With friends, you can also play with any rules you all agree on.

visual.altText: A two-player table and a four-player table.

steps.title: Standard
steps.body:
[[standard|Standard]] uses only cards from recent sets. Older sets rotate out over time, so the card pool stays fresh.

- At least **60 cards** in your deck.
- No more than **four copies** of any card, except basic lands.
- Both players start at **20 life**.

It's a good first format, and you can play it in MTG Arena, the official digital game.

visual.altText: A 60-card deck with up to four copies of a card.

check.question: In Standard, how many copies of one card (not a basic land) can your deck have?
check.hint: It's in bold in the list.

steps.title: Commander basics
steps.body:
[[commander|Commander]] is the most popular casual format. Usually four players play, each against the others.

- Your deck has exactly **100 cards**, including your commander: a legendary creature that leads the deck.
- Only **one copy** of each card, except basic lands.
- Every card must match your commander's [[color-identity|colour identity]].
- Everyone starts at **40 life**.

visual.altText: A commander beside its 99-card deck, and 40 life.

check.question: How much life does each player start with in Commander?
check.hint: 100 is the deck size, not the life total.

steps.title: Commander's special rules
steps.body:
Your commander starts in the **command zone**, not in your library. You can cast it from there whenever you could cast that creature.

- If it would go to your graveyard or into exile, you may put it back in the command zone instead.
- Each time you cast it again from the command zone, it costs {2} more.
- A player dealt **21 combat damage** by the same commander loses.

visual.altText: A commander going back to the command zone, costing 2 more next time.

check.question: Your commander was cast from the command zone once before. How much extra does it cost now?
check.hint: It's 2 more for each previous time it was cast from the command zone.

steps.title: A Commander deck recipe
steps.body:
A rough guide many players use for a 100-card Commander deck, from Tyrna's "Commander Stats" community summary:

- **36 to 38** lands
- **About 10** cards that make extra mana (ramp)
- **About 10** cards that draw extra cards
- **7 or 8** cards that remove one threat, and **about 5** that clear the whole board
- The rest support your deck's plan

These are starting points, not rules.

visual.altText: A 100-card deck split into lands, ramp, draw, removal and plan cards.

steps.title: Where to go next
steps.body:
You know the core rules now. Ways to keep learning:

- **Practise** at the Practice Table in this app, with friends, or in MTG Arena, the official digital game.
- **Visit a local game store.** Many run beginner nights. The Wizards of the Coast store locator lists them.
- **Start with a preconstructed deck**: ready to play, no building needed.

Mistakes are normal. Every player started where you are.

visual.altText: Three ways to keep playing: the app, a game store, a starter deck.
